race.name: GFNY San Luis Potosí
race.tagline: Two high-altitude laps, 154 kilometers, and 2,237 meters of climbing built around a 13-kilometer Pozuelos ascent.

vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive two-lap long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules

climate.description: San Luis Potosí sits around 1,877 meters above sea level. The official course moves between exposed city roads and the Sierra de San Miguelito, making sun, dry air, and altitude part of the energy-management problem.
challenges: Cool race morning with daytime warming

terrain.surface: Paved city and mountain roads between central San Luis Potosí, Pozuelos, and the Sierra de San Miguelito.
features: A fast city opening through the historic center
A 13-kilometer climb averaging three percent and reaching 7.9 percent
A broad descending return with Sierra views
A second full lap for long-course racers

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: A long, high-altitude, repeat-climb course with established GFNY execution and excellent city access. It lacks the history and field depth of Tier 1 flagships.

key_climbs: Pozuelos ascent: 13 km at three percent average, 7.9 percent maximum
Second-lap repeat of the Pozuelos ascent
Rolling return through San Luis Potosí
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: The second 13-kilometer Pozuelos ascent, when altitude and more than 75 kilometers of prior racing turn moderate gradients into a durability test.

course_description.character: The long course doubles a 77-kilometer circuit from San Luis Potosí's historic center. Each lap includes a 13-kilometer climb toward Pozuelos and a wide-road descent, producing 154.3 kilometers and 2,237 meters of gain at a host-city altitude near 1,877 meters. The second lap is the race.
course_description.signature_challenge: Repeating the 13-kilometer Pozuelos climb after the first circuit at altitude.

logistics.airport: San Luis Potosí International Airport (SLP) is approximately 17 kilometers from the city center and has domestic and selected international connections.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay near the historic center or along a direct route to the official race hub, then confirm current road closures and packet-pickup details.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, start access, parking, and bike transport.
logistics.food: The city center has abundant restaurants and markets; arrive early enough to normalize routine at altitude and carry practiced fuel for two full laps.

history.origin_story: GFNY launched San Luis Potosí in 2025 with a city-and-Sierra circuit built around the Pozuelos climb.
notable_moments: 2025: Inaugural edition establishes the two-lap long course
history.reputation: A substantial Mexican GFNY whose distance, altitude, and repeat climb demand dedicated preparation.

biased_opinion.summary: San Luis Potosí gives you a full preview and then asks whether you learned anything. The first lap reveals the climb, descent, altitude, and feeding rhythm. The second applies all four again after fatigue, which is why a moderate average gradient should not fool anyone.
biased_opinion.bottom_line: One of the more complete GFNY tests: long enough for endurance, high enough for altitude, and repetitive enough to expose bad pacing.

final_verdict.one_liner: Two high-altitude laps, 154 kilometers, and 2,237 meters of climbing built around a 13-kilometer Pozuelos ascent.
final_verdict.should_you_race: One of the more complete GFNY tests: long enough for endurance, high enough for altitude, and repetitive enough to expose bad pacing.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Cozumel for a flatter Mexican race, or GFNY Aguascalientes for another highland option.
